s0_title: Pact: settlement infrastructure for the agent economy, built on PayPal escrow. This is the live application, running against PayPal Sandbox.
s1_problem: Agreeing on scope, price, and payment is slow and hard to coordinate, and neither side wants to move first on money. Pact fixes that. A buyer posts a job with a brief, acceptance criteria, and a hard budget ceiling. Seller agents then compete, and an A.I. buyer counters, until they agree inside that budget. The two-hundred-dollar ceiling here is enforced in code.
s2_agreement: This is a real, completed settlement. Three seller agents quoted between one hundred and forty and one hundred and fifty dollars. The buyer countered each one, and the price converged to one hundred and twenty-five dollars, under the ceiling, with seller Atlas selected. Every message in the negotiation is recorded.
s3_payment: Now the payment flow. Pact creates a PayPal order with intent authorize, so funds are reserved, not taken. PayPal requires the buyer to approve first, so Pact surfaces that step honestly. This is the real PayPal Sandbox checkout. After approval, Pact authorizes the order, and then captures it. The escrow record shows all three PayPal objects: the order, the authorization, and the capture id.
s4_safety: Before any capture, an independent verifier checks the delivery against every acceptance criterion. The verification panel reports passed, score one point zero zero, with evidence that all acceptance criteria are met. Deterministic checks and model judgement are combined, so a confident-sounding but empty delivery cannot pass. Capture happens only after a passing verdict. A failed verification voids the authorization instead, and duplicate or concurrent requests can never capture the same authorization twice.
s5_ledger: Every decision lands in a hash-chained ledger. Each entry stores the hash of the one before it, so editing any historical row breaks the chain, and the interface verifies it live. Reputation is what makes this more than a payment wrapper: a seller with a poor record must be substantially cheaper to win the next job, so the market routes around unreliable sellers on its own.
s6_close: That is Pact: A.I.-assisted negotiation, conditional PayPal settlement, and a tamper-evident record, running on PayPal Sandbox, with a live A.I. model and durable Postgres storage.
